cards.a: An alternative to route reflectors for scaling iBGP: the AS is split into sub-ASes that peer with each other using eBGP-like sessions while presenting a single confederation AS to the outside world. It reduces the iBGP full-mesh burden, though it is rarer in the exam than reflectors.

cards.q: How do confederation and route reflector differ?
cards.a: Route reflector is a hub-and-spoke model with clients guarded by ORIGINATOR_ID and CLUSTER_LIST; confederation splits the AS into eBGP-style sub-ASes guarded by the confederation AS_PATH subset. Confederation needs a sub-AS split, appears less often in the exam, and both lose no attributes.

cards.q: What AD do confederation eBGP sessions use?
cards.a: AD 200, like iBGP, not 20. iBGP within a sub-AS uses AD 200, confederation eBGP (other sub-AS) uses AD 200 with eBGP-like behavior but attributes kept, and only real eBGP with an outside AS uses AD 20.

cards.q: Which attributes survive confederation sub-AS boundaries?
cards.a: Local-pref, MED, and next-hop are preserved across sub-AS boundaries, unlike with real eBGP. Next hop is not changed between sub-ASes (unless next-hop-self is needed for real eBGP), and AS_PATH is extended with the confederation sequence that is stripped before the route leaves to the real world.

cards.q: How do you configure a confederation?
cards.a: router bgp 64512 with bgp confederation identifier 65001 giving the public AS, bgp confederation peers 64513 64514 listing the other sub-ASes, and neighbor 10.0.0.2 remote-as 64513 for the confederation eBGP peer.

cards.q: How does a confederation prevent loops?
cards.a: Confederation sub-ASes appear in the confederation sequence, and a route carrying your confederation ID in the confed part is rejected. The confederation sequence is stripped at the real eBGP boundary, so outsiders see a clean AS_PATH of real ASes.

cards.q: When should you choose confederation over route reflectors?
cards.a: When the AS is already segmented by policy or geography and you want eBGP-like boundary control without changing attributes. Otherwise route reflectors are simpler to operate.

cards.q: Do local-pref, MED, and next-hop change across sub-AS boundaries?
cards.a: No, they are preserved, unlike real eBGP. This is the key exam distinction between confederation peers and true external eBGP peers.

cards.q: What does the outside world see in the AS_PATH from a confederation?
cards.a: Only the confederation identifier. The confederation sequence of sub-ASes is stripped before the route is advertised to a real eBGP neighbor.

Model of sub-ASes; confed eBGP AD is 200; attributes preserved; public AS is the confederation identifier; the sub-AS list is confederation peers; loop guard is the confed AS_PATH; the outside view has confed ASes stripped; alternative is route reflector.
